title: Ordinary pullback of principal Koszul towers and target augmentation
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $t$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites put $R_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}S_{W,n}$, $S_{W,n}=(A/t^n)_W$, with specified projections $\pi_{W,n}$ and quotient transitions $q_{n+1,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. All finite levels are restricted along these projections. Write $c_g:g^{-1}R_T\to R_{T'}$ for the projection-induced ring map and $G(M)=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}R_T}R_{T'}$ for ordinary module pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Use unbounded cochain complexes and their derived localizations $Q$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A good complex means K-flat with flat terms [def-a1-flat-term-kflat-complex]. Set $Q_{W,n}=[R_W\xrightarrow{t^n}R_W]$ in degrees $-1,0$, with transition $(t,1)$ and augmentation $\epsilon_{W,n}:Q_{W,n}\to S_{W,n}[0]$ equal to $\pi_{W,n}$ in degree zero and zero in degree minus one [def-a1-principal-completed-koszul-towers].

For every good $R_T$-complex $P$, the complexes $GP$ and $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})$ are good for every $n$. There is a natural isomorphism of strict towers of cochain complexes
$$\theta_P:(G(P\otimes Q_{T,n}))_n\xrightarrow{\sim}(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n.$$
It is the ordinary cochain tensor comparison followed by the action unitor $GR_T\cong R_{T'}$ on each of the two Koszul terms. On a local tensor, $G(P\otimes Q_{T,n})$ is written with elements $(x\otimes e_i)\otimes b$, where $e_i$ is the unit basis of $Q_{T,n}^i$ for $i=-1,0$; its image is $(x\otimes b)\otimes e'_i$ in the corresponding reindexed total summand. In particular $G(t^n)$ is multiplication by $t^n$, and $\theta_P$ intertwines the source transition $G(1_P\otimes(t,1))$ with $1_{GP}\otimes(t,1)$, without a scalar or sign adjustment.

The target quotient augmentation
$$a_{GP}=(1_{GP}\otimes\epsilon_{T',n})_n:(GP\otimes Q_{T',n})_n\longrightarrow(GP\otimes S_{T',n})_n$$
is a strict tower morphism whose every level is a quasi-isomorphism, hence a quasi-isomorphism of complexes in the strict tower category $\operatorname{Tow}_{R_{T'}}=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op},\operatorname{Mod}(R_{T'}))$, whose exactness is levelwise [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Both $\theta_P$ and $a_{GP}$ are natural for chain maps $P\to P'$ between good complexes. This does not assert that $G$ preserves arbitrary quasi-isomorphisms: the augmentation here is the one over the target completed ring. The structural map $c_g$ need not be flat or invertible.

proof.text: Apply lem-a1-principal-koszul-strict-replacement on Y to P. Its last two conclusions give goodness of every H_Y(P)_n; the preservation result from step 2 gives goodness after applying G. Apply the same replacement theorem on X to GP, using step 2. Its first conclusion is exactly the levelwise quasi-isomorphism of the target comparison augmentation. Its existing comparison_naturality theorem gives the final strict chain-map naturality equation.

Apply Mathlib HomologicalComplex.quasiIso_iff_evaluation to transpose.map of the target comparison. By the concrete transpose definition, its evaluation at n is definitionally the level augmentation of step 3. That augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism for each n, so the transposed comparison is a quasi-isomorphism. This is the levelwise-homology argument of the original proof, and never applies G to an arbitrary source quasi-isomorphism.
